html:
The White River and Kluane First Nations are Athabaskan peoples of southwest Yukon, around Kluane Lake and the White River near the border with Alaska. The Kluane people speak Southern Tutchone; the White River people speak Upper Tanana and Northern Tutchone.

They lived by hunting caribou, moose and Dall sheep, trapping, and fishing in the lakes and rivers, and they traded copper and furs with the Tlingit of the coast. The Klondike Gold Rush of 1896 to 1899 and a Kluane gold rush in 1903 brought outsiders, and the Alaska Highway, built through Burwash Landing and Beaver Creek in 1942, changed their land for good. The creation of Kluane National Park in 1972 shut them out of hunting grounds until later land claims. The map also has a separate Kluane territory, and their neighbours to the east include the Tagish.
